description: Hosted Reverse Shell generator with a ton of functionality. -- (Great for CTFs)

summary.one_liner: A hosted web-based reverse shell generator that builds common reverse shell payloads and listener commands, aimed at CTF players.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a browser-based tool for generating reverse shell payloads and common listeners. It offers a button to save generated payloads for download and a raw mode that produces cURL-based shells pointing at your machine. Users can increment the listening port with a single button and apply URI or Base64 encoding to output. Configuration persists in LocalStorage, and the interface has dark, light and meme color modes. It also lists a HoaxShell integration with a custom listener, though the README links to separate docs for that feature. The project can be run locally with Netlify dev or a Docker container.
use_cases: generate reverse shell payloads for a CTF challenge
create a netcat or other listener command
Base64 or URL-encode a shell payload
quickly increment listener port between attempts
download generated payloads from the browser
run a private reverse shell generator in Docker
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into it
Browse to the local address shown in the README (port 80 mapping)
For modifying server functions: npx netlify dev
notable: Raw mode that produces cURL-based reverse shells
HoaxShell integration with a custom listener
URI and Base64 encoding of payloads
caveats: README does not document the list of supported shell types or languages in detail
Server-side features such as raw link support depend on running under netlify dev
HoaxShell details are only linked externally, not explained in the README
